findings.title: Information Disclosure: Stack Traces and Error Details
findings.description: Multiple endpoints return verbose error messages and stack traces containing sensitive information including: file paths (/juice-shop/build/routes/), framework versions (Express, Sequelize), database details (SQLite), and internal logic. These error messages leak the application structure and can aid attackers in identifying further vulnerabilities. CWE-209 (Information Exposure Through an Error Message). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N (5.3 MEDIUM).
steps: Observe 500 response with full stack trace
Stack trace reveals: file path /juice-shop/build/routes/orderHistory.js:43, framework express, ORM sequelize, database SQLite
findings.evidence: HTTP 500 GET /rest/order-history returned stack trace with /juice-shop/build/routes/orderHistory.js:43:18, express/lib/router/layer.js, sequelize/lib/dialects paths

findings.title: CORS Misconfiguration: Wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin
findings.description: All API endpoints return 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' header, allowing requests from any origin. When combined with credentials via JWT authentication, this can enable Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks. An attacker-controlled webpage can make authenticated requests on behalf of a victim user. CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N (7.1 HIGH).
steps: Create attacker webpage with XMLHttpRequest to API endpoints
Victim visits attacker page while authenticated to Juice Shop
Malicious requests execute with victim's JWT credentials
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 response headers include: access-control-allow-origin:* on endpoints like /rest/admin/application-version, /api/Feedbacks/, /api/Users/, /rest/basket/1

findings.title: SQL Injection in User Login (Authentication Bypass)
findings.description: The POST /rest/user/login endpoint is vulnerable to SQL injection in the 'email' parameter. Attacker can bypass authentication by sending payload ' OR '1'='1' --, which returns valid JWT token for admin user (ID 1, admin@juice-sh.op). Complete authentication bypass enabling unauthorized administrative access. CWE-89 (SQL Injection). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H (9.8 CRITICAL).
steps: Receive 200 OK with valid JWT for admin@juice-sh.op (ID 1, role: admin)
Use JWT to access restricted endpoints and perform admin actions
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 POST /rest/user/login with SQL injection payload returned JWT token with role:admin, email:admin@juice-sh.op, ID:1, password hash in payload

findings.title: Mass Assignment: Privilege Escalation via Role Parameter
findings.description: POST /api/Users/ endpoint accepts and stores arbitrary fields without whitelist validation, including 'role' and 'isAdmin'. Attacker can create new user account with role='admin' directly, bypassing all authentication and authorization. Immediate privilege escalation to administrative level without credentials. CWE-915 (Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N (8.6 HIGH).
steps: Receive 201 Created with role:admin confirmed in response body
Login with created admin credentials for full system access
findings.evidence: HTTP 201 POST /api/Users/ returned user object: id:23, email:admin_test@test.com, role:admin, profileImage:/assets/public/images/uploads/defaultAdmin.png, confirming mass assignment of admin role

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in Basket Access
findings.description: GET /rest/basket/<id> endpoint lacks proper access control, allowing any authenticated user to access baskets of other users by manipulating the id parameter. User ID 2 (jim@juice-sh.op) successfully retrieved complete basket contents of user ID 1, including product details, quantities, and pricing. Enables unauthorized horizontal privilege escalation and sensitive data exfiltration. CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N (7.5 HIGH).
steps: Authenticate as user jim@juice-sh.op (ID 2) with provided JWT
Observe response contains UserId:1 with products Apple Juice (qty 2) and Orange Juice (qty 3)
Verify data belongs to user ID 1, not authenticated user ID 2
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 GET /rest/basket/1 (authenticated as user ID 2) returned: {id:1, UserId:1, Products:[{id:1, name:Apple Juice, quantity:2}, {id:2, name:Orange Juice, quantity:3}]}

findings.title: CAPTCHA Bypass: Answer Exposed in Response
findings.description: GET /rest/captcha endpoint returns both the CAPTCHA challenge and its correct answer in the same response. Any client can immediately obtain correct answer without solving challenge. Bypasses rate limiting and account protection mechanisms relying on CAPTCHA. CWE-640 (Weak Password Recovery Mechanism Using Question and Answer). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N (6.5 MEDIUM).
steps: Use answer value in POST /api/Feedbacks/ with captchaId:1, captcha:"99"

findings.title: Information Disclosure: Sensitive Configuration Exposed
findings.description: GET /rest/admin/application-configuration exposes detailed configuration without authentication: server port (3000), base URL, domain (juice-sh.op), database version (3.44.0), feature flags. Information aids reconnaissance. CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N (5.3 MEDIUM).
steps: Observe configuration including port, domain, databaseVersion, feature flags

findings.title: Bypass de Validação de Rating — Zero Estrelas
findings.description: É possível submeter avaliações com rating 0 (inválido pela UI) diretamente via API. O backend não valida o intervalo permitido (1–5), confiando apenas na validação do frontend Angular.

findings.title: [ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: [ZAP] X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
findings.description: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps:
Solução: Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session ID in URL Rewrite

findings.title: [ZAP] Re-examine Cache-control Directives
findings.description: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached. | CWE-525 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".

findings.title: [ZAP] Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797. | CWE-319 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

Being a web application with a vast number of intended security vulnerabilities, the OWASP Juice Shop is supposed to be the opposite of a best practice or template application for web develop

steps.thought:
Excelente. A página `/administration` carregou com HTML/JS, mas Angular executou lógica client-side que apresenta mensagem **403 "You are not allowed to access this page!"**. Isso indica que há proteção no frontend (verificação de role/permissão), não no backend. O HTML foi servido sem autenticação, mas o conteúdo foi protegido por JavaScript.

**Achado:** Broken Access Control via client-side enforcement apenas — a página HTML é acessível, apenas a renderização foi bloqueada. Isso sugere que a API backend pode estar desprotegida ou protegida apenas por verificação de token JWT que posso contornar.

Vou agora testar endpoints administrativos da API diretamente, sem autenticação e com técnicas de bypass (JWT mal validado, HTTP verb tampering, etc.).

---
`/api/Users/` requer autenticação (401). Bom — proteção presente. Vou testar com JWT fornecido e depois focar em outros endpoints. Continuando com as requisições pendentes.

`/rest/continue-code` retorna um token de continuação sem autenticação. Token parece ser base64 ou string aleatória de 64 caracteres. Vou decodificar e verificar se é previsível (candidato a predição de token). Por enquanto, armazenar como info útil. Continuar com próximas requisições.

`/api/Feedbacks/` retorna lista pública de feedbacks com `UserId`, `id`, `comment`, `rating`, timestamps. Dados sensíveis: emails parcialmente mascarados (padrão `***`), mas ainda identificáveis. Não vejo XSS payloads nos comentários existentes (sanitizados ou não armazenados). Vou testar POST com XSS para confirmar. Continuar com IDOR em basket.

**ACHADO CRÍTICO — IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference)**

Usuário ID 2 (jim@juice-sh.op) conseguiu acessar basket ID 1 (que pertence a usuário ID 1) usando apenas JWT e alteração do ID na URL. A resposta retorna:
- `UserId: 1` (confirma que é basket de outro usuário)
- Produtos completos no carrinho (Apple Juice qty 2, Orange Juice qty 3)
- Preços (incluindo `deluxePrice` — pode indicar manipulação de preço possível)

**CVSS 3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N** (7.5 HIGH — escalada horizontal de leitura)

Este é escalação de privilégio via IDOR. Vou testar PUT/PATCH para confirmar se é também de escrita (crítico para manipular preços ou quantidades).

---

**Achado de info disclosure — Stack trace vaza:**
- Banco de dados: SQLite (Sequelize ORM)
- Estrutura: `/juice-shop/build/routes/captcha.js:33:25`
- Erro lógico: `captchaId` undefined ao criar feedback (indica que feedback requer CAPTCHA, mas POST direto não fornece)

**CWE-209 (Information Exposure Through an Error Message), CVSS 3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N** (5.3 MEDIUM)

A criação de feedback requer CAPTCHA. Vou tentar contornar obtendo captchaId primeiro ou testando se há bypass.

---

**ACHADO CRÍTICO — Mass Assignment / Over-posting (CWE-915)**

POST `/api/Users/` com `role: "admin"` foi aceito e criou usuário com `role: "admin"` diretamente. Resposta confirma:
- `id: 23`
- `email: admin_test@test.com`
- `role: "admin"` ← **VULNERABILIDADE CRÍTICA**
- `profileImage: /assets/public/images/uploads/defaultAdmin.png` ← Indica elevação de privilégio

**CVSS 3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N** (8.6 HIGH — escalada vertical, account takeover potencial)

Este é um achado CRÍTICO: qualquer usuário anônimo pode criar conta admin. Combinado com IDOR de basket, forma cadeia de privilege escalation.

Vou agora fazer login com essa conta admin e testar endpoints administrativos.

---

**CONFIRMADO — Escalada vertical via Mass Assignment + Login bem-sucedido**

Login com `admin_test@test.com` / `password123` retornou JWT com `role: "admin"`. Dados expostos no JWT (CWE-347):
- `id: 23`
- `role: "admin"`
- `password: "482c811da5d5b4bc6d497ffa98491e38"` (MD5 hash visível em JWT!)
- `profileImage: /assets/public/images/uploads/defaultAdmin.png`

**ACHADO: Credenciais sensíveis expostas em JWT (CWE-347, CWE-200)**

Agora tenho JWT admin. Vou testar acesso a endpoints administrativos. Continuar cobertura de outras categorias.

---

**ACHADO CRÍTICO — SQL Injection em Login**

O payload `' OR '1'='1' --` no campo email retornou sucesso com login como `admin@juice-sh.op` (admin real do sistema, ID 1). Isso confirma:

**SQL Injection (CWE-89) em `/rest/user/login`**
- Endpoint: POST `/rest/user/login`
- Parâmetro: `email`
- Payload: `' OR '1'='1' --`
- Resultado: Autenticação bypass — retornou JWT válido para admin (ID 1)
- **CVSS 3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H** (9.8 CRITICAL — autenticação bypass total)

JWT obtido contém credenciais sensíveis novamente (`password` hash em claro, `role: admin`).

Agora tenho dois JWTs admin (ID 1 e ID 23). Vou usar para testar endpoints administrativos e continuar cobertura de categorias.

Agora posso criar feedback sem limiar CAPTCHA. Continuar com testes.

**ACHADO — HTTP Verb Tampering / CORS Misconfiguration**

OPTIONS `/rest/basket/1` retorna 204 com headers:
- `access-control-allow-methods: GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE` — todos os verbos permitidos
- `access-control-allow-origin: *` — CORS aberto

Isso sugere que PUT/PATCH/POST/DELETE podem ser suportados em `/rest/basket/1`, mas as tentativas anteriores retornaram 500 "Unexpected path". Isso indica um **routing issue** — o middleware Angular está interceptando e rejeitando, não o endpoint em si.

Continuar com testes finais.

action.description: GET /rest/basket/<id> endpoint lacks proper access control, allowing any authenticated user to access baskets of other users by manipulating the id parameter.
